# PART 2 — CONFLICTING OR AMBIGUOUS AUTHORITIES

- **Non-tiered waiver routing inconsistency across publications**: Multiple AFIs define different routing for non-tiered compliance item waivers. Some route to the "requestor's commander" (AFI 36-1301, AFI 36-2113, DAFI 31-126), others to the "AFGM OPR" (AFGM 2026-36-2033), others to AFPC/DPM via MAJCOM (AFI 36-2122), others to AFPC/DP3AM via MAJCOM (AFI 36-2135), others to AFPC/DPPSP with AF/A1P concurrence (AFI 36-2406), others to the CMSAF (AFI 36-2109), and others to the "publication OPR" (AFI 36-2129). There is no single standard for non-tiered waiver approval. — See AFGM 2026-36-2033 vs AFI 36-1301 vs AFI 36-2109 vs AFI 36-2113 vs AFI 36-2122 vs AFI 36-2129 vs AFI 36-2135 vs AFI 36-2406 vs DAFI 31-126.

- **Ambiguous "approval authority" for 8F000 SDI beyond-four-years and cross-SDI applications**: AFI 36-2113 §2.1.14 and §2.1.15 reference an unnamed entity that "serves as the approval authority" for RegAF requests to serve beyond four years in the 8F000 SDI and for cross-SDI applications. The specific role/office is not identified in the extracted statements, making delegation unclear. — See AFI 36-2113 §2.1.14 and §2.1.15.

- **Overlapping authority for key leadership position waivers**: AFI 36-1301 assigns the SAE authority to approve position and tenure waivers for specific acquisition positions, while also assigning "the appropriate senior level official within the command" authority over all other key leadership positions. The boundary between SAE-controlled positions and command-level positions may be ambiguous for positions not explicitly listed. — See AFI 36-1301 (multiple sections on position/tenure waivers).

- **CSAF vs. HAF Deputy Chief of Staff, Personnel for evaluation exceptions**: AFI 36-2406 states "Only the CSAF may approve exceptions," but then grants "similar authority" to the HAF Deputy Chief of Staff, Personnel for general officer management cases. The scope of "similar authority" and whether this constitutes a formal delegation or a parallel grant is unclear. — See AFI 36-2406 (exceptions section).

- **Over-grade approval authority during rotation**: AFI 36-2113 §6.4.7 references "recommendation by the CCM, approval authority, WG/CC or equivalent" but it is ambiguous whether the "approval authority" is a separate entity from WG/CC or if WG/CC is the approval authority. The comma-separated list creates uncertainty about the chain. — See AFI 36-2113 §6.4.7.

- **Wing Commander escalation vs. initial approval authority**: AFI 36-2406 provides that if an "approval authority" recommends disapproval, the request escalates to the wing commander. The identity of the initial "approval authority" at a lower level is not specified in the extracted statement, creating ambiguity about who makes the initial determination. — See AFI 36-2406 (disapproval escalation section).

- **AFPC MLR Office vs. ARPC/PB for pre-board evaluation changes**: Both offices can approve changes up to one duty day prior to a central selection board under "extreme circumstances," but the distinction between their jurisdictions (RegAF vs. ARC) is implied rather than explicit in the extracted text. — See AFI 36-2406 (pre-board changes sections).

# PART 3 — AUTHORITY GAPS

- **12 Outstanding Airmen of the Year (12 OAY) selection authority**: AFI 36-2109 establishes that the publication addresses selection and approval authority for CMSAF, CCM, and group SEL positions, and mentions 12 OAY travel entitlements, but no extracted statement identifies who has the authority to select or approve 12 OAY recipients.

- **Waiver authority for mandatory training requirements (military members) under DAFI 31-118**: The document references "Waiver Authority for Mandatory Training Requirements—Civilians" (Table 6.2) and general waiver tables, but no extracted statement identifies the specific waiver authority for **military member** mandatory training requirements, only civilian.

- **Authority to establish or modify SB, SWG, SFTWG, EWG, and SFEC membership**: While chairs of these bodies retain authority over "permanent voting membership changes," no statement identifies who has the authority to initially establish membership, set the charter, or appoint the chairs themselves.

- **Authority to approve or disapprove pre-accession religious accommodation denials**: AFGM 2026-36-2033 states "the AF will approve" accommodations unless military necessity is adversely affected, but does not specify which role/office makes the determination that military necessity is adversely affected or who has final denial authority.

- **Authority to define "extreme circumstances" for pre-board evaluation changes**: Both AFPC MLR Office and ARPC/PB may approve changes under "extreme circumstances," but no authority is identified for defining or adjudicating what qualifies as "extreme circumstances."

- **Authority to approve EPW personal effects beyond the 55-pound limit**: AFJI 31-304 notes certain items are excluded from the 55-pound limit but does not identify who has the authority to adjudicate disputes about what qualifies as excluded items or to approve additional personal effects.

- **Waiver authority for DAFI 31-118 civilian training requirements (specific approving official)**: The document references Tables 6.1 and 6.2 for approval authority and procedures, and mentions HQ AF/A4S/CFM as a default, but the specific tier-by-tier breakdown of who approves at each level (unit, MAJCOM, HAF) is not fully articulated in the extracted statements.

- **Authority over CCB actions when CCB Chairperson is unavailable and no designated representative has been named**: DAFI 31-126 states only the CCB Chairperson or designated representative may approve/disapprove CCB actions, but no succession or contingency authority is identified if both are unavailable.
